## Introduction

RDBESvisualise summarises and visualises data in the RDBES format. All
functions take an `RDBESDataObject` created with
`RDBEScore::createRDBESDataObject()`, check it and return a table or a plot.

This vignette shows one example for each exported function. It uses the
example data of the RDBEScore package, which are test data and not real
sampling data:

| Data | Hierarchy | Main tables with data |
|:-----|:----------|:----------------------|
| `H1Example` | 1 | DE, SD, VS, FT, FO, SS, SA, FM, BV, VD |
| `H5Example` | 5 | DE, SD, FT, OS, LE, SS, SA, FM, BV, VD, CL, CE |
| `H7Example` | 7 | DE, SD, OS, LE, SS, SA, BV |
| `H8ExampleEE1` | 8 | DE, SD, VS, TE, LE, SS, SA, BV, VD, CL, CE |

The functions are:

| Topic | Function |
|:------|:---------|
| Amounts by group | `amountByGroup()` |
| Sampling design | `summariseSelectionMethod()`, `summariseSampledNonSampled()` |
| Biological variables | `summariseBiologicalVariables()` |
| Sampling coverage | `produceSamplingCoverage()`, `coverageBySpecies()`, `coverageByGear()`, `coverageTemporal()`, `coverageSpatial()`, `coverageSpatialBivariate()` |

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(RDBESvisualise)
library(RDBEScore)
```

## Amounts by group

`amountByGroup()` sums numeric variables and counts categorical variables by
one or more grouping variables. With an `RDBESDataObject` the table is chosen
from the prefix of the first variable, here the landings (CL).

```{r amountByGroup}
landings <- amountByGroup(H8ExampleEE1,
  var = "CLoffWeight",
  valBy = c("CLquar", "CLvesLenCat"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
landings
```

## Sampling design

`summariseSelectionMethod()` shows the percentage of the units selected with
each selection method, by table.

```{r selectionMethod}
summariseSelectionMethod(H1Example, output_type = "table")
summariseSelectionMethod(H1Example)
```

`summariseSampledNonSampled()` shows the percentage of the units that were
sampled and, for the units that were not sampled, the reasons. Missing or
empty values are shown as "(missing)": in this example data no reason is
given for the species that were not sampled.

```{r sampledNonSampled}
summariseSampledNonSampled(H1Example)
```

## Biological variables

`summariseBiologicalVariables()` counts the individuals with each type of
measurement and summarises the values. Length, weight and age are summarised
as numbers, sex and maturity as categories. The data can be split by any
column of the tables above BV, for example by species.

```{r biologicalTable}
summariseBiologicalVariables(H7Example, by = "SAspeCode")
```

With `output_type = "plot"` the function returns one plot per type of
measurement.

```{r biologicalPlot}
bioPlots <- summariseBiologicalVariables(H7Example,
  var = c("Length", "Maturity"),
  by = "SAspeCode",
  output_type = "plot"
)
bioPlots$LengthTotal
bioPlots$Maturity
```

## Sampling coverage

The coverage functions compare the samples with the landings (CL) or the
effort (CE). Their relative values show where much is landed or fished but
little is sampled.

The sample date is taken from the first of FO, FT, LE and OS that has a date.
The rectangle, area and gear of a sample are taken from FO or LE if they are
missing in SA. Hierarchy 8, which has no FO table, can therefore be used.
Samples without any date only have the year (`DEyear`).

If the variable to sum has missing values these records are excluded from
the relative values and a warning says how many are missing. In
`H8ExampleEE1`, `SAsampWtLive` is missing for all samples:

```{r missingValues}
coverageTable <- produceSamplingCoverage(H8ExampleEE1,
  var = "SAsampWtLive",
  contrastVar = "CLoffWeight",
  resolution = "Quarter",
  catchCat = "Lan",
  output_type = "table"
)
```

The examples below therefore use the measured sample weight `SAsampWtMes`.

### produceSamplingCoverage

`produceSamplingCoverage()` sums the sampling and the landings or effort at
one resolution: "ICES Rectangle", "ICES Area", "Year", "Semester",
"Quarter", "Month", "Gear", "Vessel length" or "Species". `by` splits the
data further, and the relative values are then calculated within each level
of `by`.

```{r produceSamplingCoverageTable}
produceSamplingCoverage(H8ExampleEE1,
  var = "SAsampWtMes",
  contrastVar = "CLoffWeight",
  resolution = "Quarter",
  catchCat = "Lan",
  output_type = "table"
)
```

```{r produceSamplingCoverageBar}
produceSamplingCoverage(H8ExampleEE1,
  var = "SAamountSamp",
  contrastVar = "CEnumFracTrips",
  resolution = "Vessel length",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
```

For "ICES Rectangle" and "ICES Area" the result is a map. The colour shows
the landings or effort and the circles show the sampling. Numbers are shown
without scientific notation.

```{r produceSamplingCoverageMap, fig.height = 6}
produceSamplingCoverage(H8ExampleEE1,
  var = "SAsampWtMes",
  contrastVar = "CLoffWeight",
  resolution = "ICES Rectangle",
  by = "Quarter",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
```

```{r produceSamplingCoverageArea, warning = FALSE}
produceSamplingCoverage(H5Example,
  var = "SAamountSamp",
  contrastVar = "CLoffWeight",
  resolution = "ICES Area",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
```

### Interactive coverage plots

The `coverageXXX()` functions return a list of interactive plots, one per
year (the spatial functions need a single year). The title states that
`catchCat` refers to the sample data only.

```{r coverageBySpecies}
speciesPlots <- coverageBySpecies(H8ExampleEE1,
  year = 2022,
  vesselFlag = "ZW",
  landingsVariable = "CLoffWeight",
  samplingVariable = "SAsampWtMes",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
speciesPlots[[1]]
```

```{r coverageByGear}
gearPlots <- coverageByGear(H8ExampleEE1,
  year = 2022,
  landingsVariable = "CLoffWeight",
  effortVariable = "CEnumFracTrips",
  samplingVariable = "SAsampWtMes",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
gearPlots[[1]]
```

```{r coverageTemporal, warning = FALSE}
temporalPlots <- coverageTemporal(H8ExampleEE1,
  year = 2022,
  landingsVariable = "CLoffWeight",
  effortVariable = "CEnumFracTrips",
  samplingVariable = "SAsampWtMes",
  catchCat = "Lan"
)
temporalPlots[[1]]
```

The spatial maps only draw the area around the data, which keeps them fast.

```{r coverageSpatial, message = FALSE}
spatialPlots <- coverageSpatial(H8ExampleEE1,
  year = 2022,
  landingsVariable = "CLoffWeight",
  samplingVariable = "SAsampWtMes",
  catchCat = "Lan",
  includeEffort = FALSE
)
spatialPlots[[1]]
```

```{r coverageSpatialBivariate, warning = FALSE}
bivariatePlots <- coverageSpatialBivariate(H8ExampleEE1,
  year = 2022,
  landingsVariable = "CLoffWeight",
  samplingVariable = "SAsampWtMes",
  catchCat = "Lan",
  includeEffort = FALSE
)
bivariatePlots[[1]]
```

## Colours and spatial levels

Plots use the RCG palette and then the colours of `colourPalette`, which
also gives each country a fixed colour.

```{r palette}
colourPalette[c("EE", "LV", "LT", "PL")]
```

`icesStatRecLookup` links each ICES rectangle to its ICES area and RCG region.
The internal function `rectanglesToRegions()` uses it to convert codes.

```{r regions}
icesStatRecLookup[icesStatRecLookup$StatRec %in% c("44H2", "44H3", "45H3"), ]
RDBESvisualise:::rectanglesToRegions(c("44H2", "41F6", "27.7.e"), to = "Region")
```

  Annex A3.5. <https://doi.org/10.17895/ices.pub.7915>
